subject: Fee-swap request + capacity top-up — routing to legal
messages:
From: Marta Soler <marta.soler@pulsehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: PulseHealth Procurement <procure@pulsehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Request: fee-swap + capacity top-up (PulseHealth)

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the architecture look great. We need to accelerate capacity for a pilot that launches in September. Our procurement team asked me to reach out to see if Redwood can: 1) add ~200 reserved GPU units to our Dedicated pool for a 3-month ramp and 2) accept a fee-swap where we convert a portion of our existing credits into an implementation/throughput credit to cover month 1-3 operational delta.

High level ask:
- Effective 9/1: +200 GPUs (reserved) for 3 months, then revisit.
- No change to MSA term length; this would be an order-form level change or small amendment.
- We prefer not to do an immediate invoice; proposal is to reallocate $XXX,XXX in existing credits to cover first quarter and then settle normal billing starting month 4.

Can you route this to legal for a light redline and confirm whether an Exhibit (egress/implementation) will be needed? I attached the current PO/credit summary. Procurement would like a signed amendment by 8/22 to hit engineering timelines.

Attachments: Pulse_PO_credits_2025Q2.pdf

Thanks,
Marta
Marta Soler
Head of Platform Partnerships 
PulseHealth

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Soler <marta.soler@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 11:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: fee-swap + capacity top-up (PulseHealth)

Hi Marta —

Appreciate the clear ask and the timeline. Looping in Ben (commercial) and will bring Laura in for legal redlines. Quick plan:
- Ben and I will propose a fee-swap structure that uses the credit pool for months 1–3 and converts to standard consumption billing month 4 onward.
- Laura will confirm whether a short amendment to the order form is sufficient or if we should add a one-off Exhibit for implementation/egress.
- We can target a signed amendment by 8/21 if legal has the redline back by 8/18.

Ben — can you draft the commercial terms (sheet attached) and include an explicit clause for rollback if capacity utilization < 30% in month 3? Marta — thanks for the PO summary, that helps.

Best,
Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: summary-commercial-notes-20250812.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Marta Soler <marta.soler@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 14:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Fee-swap proposal + suggested contract language

Jordan / Marta —

Thanks — attaching a short commercial model (proposed_fee_swap_20250812.xlsx) with two options:
Option A (preferred): Convert $300k of existing credits to a 3-month implementation/throughput credit that covers reserved capacity for the pilot. Redwood recognizes the credit as offset against upfront implementation fees; normal consumption billing resumes month 4.
Option B: 50% credit conversion + 50% deferred invoice with 60-day payment terms.

Suggested redline language (for legal to convert into amendment):
"For the period commencing 2025-09-01 and ending 2025-11-30, the Parties agree to: (i) add Two Hundred (200) Reserved GPU Units to Customer's Dedicated Pool; and (ii) reallocate $300,000 of Customer's existing Redwood credits to be applied as Implementation Credits covering the first three billing periods following the effective date. If average utilization of the Added Reserved Units is below thirty percent (30%) during the third month, Customer may request a pro rata rollback and reconciliation as set forth in Exhibit H."

I also recommend we include a short implementation Exhibit covering provisioning lead-times, acceptance criteria, and egress expectations (small table). Laura — if you can convert the above into formal amendment language I think we can get signoff.

Attachments: proposed_fee_swap_20250812.xlsx

Cheers,
Ben
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marta Soler <marta.soler@pulsehealth.com>, procure@pulsehealth.com
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: fee-swap + capacity top-up (PulseHealth) — MSA redlines attached

Jordan / Ben / Marta —

Thanks for the draft language and the context. I reviewed the proposed commercial approach and prepared a light redline to the MSA and an amendment template that encapsulates the fee-swap and the temporary capacity add. Key legal notes:
- We will implement the change as a one-page amendment to the order form (no MSA term extension).
- Added Exhibit: "Temporary Capacity Addendum" that defines provisioning SLA (72 hours for reserved pool allocation), acceptance tests, and the 30% rollback metric.
- Egress: kept existing egress terms, added a short table to call out expected monthly egress for the added units; if egress exceeds projected threshold, additional charges will apply per ratecard.
- Credit conversion: redline makes conversion explicit and time-bound; Redwood will apply the converted credits as Implementation Credits and will not issue an additional invoice for months 1–3.

I've attached: Pulse_MSA_redline_20250812.docx (with inline comments) and a clean amendment template — please review.

Marta — if acceptable I can send the DocuSign envelope today; procurement requested 8/22 sign-off but we can push to 8/21 if you confirm.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Pulse_MSA_redline_20250812.docx
